title: PAR-126 direct DWG TABLE encoder refusal
mode: Generated six-version local fast implementation slice

localScope.worktreeState: The shared worktree was already broadly modified and untracked. This slice adds a DRW_Table encoder refusal, its generated regression, plan updates, and this receipt. Nothing was staged or committed.

research.source: Open Design Specification for .dwg files, v5.4.1, section 20.4.96 (ACAD_TABLE)
research.finding: TABLE has a distinct object layout and version transition to TABLECONTENT; DRW_Table inheriting INSERT encoding can produce an INSERT/MINSERT-shaped frame that silently omits TABLE-specific content.
research.evidenceCeiling: The ODA layout supports refusing the wrong encoder path; it does not provide a completed, tested local TABLE writer implementation. No version-specific TABLE output is claimed.

implementation.change: Add a DRW_Table::encodeDwg override that returns false without changing the entity or supplied data, string, or handle buffers. Preserve the existing higher-level transactional refusal in dwgRW::writeTable.
assertions: Direct encoding refuses on all six writer versions.
Entity type, handle, and semantic-content state remain unchanged.
Data, string, and handle buffers retain their seeded bytes and healthy state.
The existing high-level save refusal still preserves the destination, reports the unsupported-table diagnostic, and allows following ordinary INSERT/LINE callbacks to be individually written.
implementation.claimBoundary: Fail-closed identity protection only. Versioned TABLE/TABLECONTENT frames, anonymous display block, linked-object graph, readback, and native acceptance remain unimplemented or unqualified.

implementationReadiness.completedSlice: Direct lower-level TABLE encoding can no longer fall through to INSERT/MINSERT encoding; all supplied output buffers remain untouched on refusal.
implementationReadiness.remainingLocalWork: Implement complete versioned TABLE/TABLECONTENT frame and linked-object graph only from ODA v5.4.1 layouts plus empirical producer traces, with independent readback and explicit failure/atomic-publication controls.
implementationReadiness.nextAction: Self-unblock to the next dependency-ready local implementation slice; do not wait for external/native qualification.
